title: How close can seven cards get to five big targets?
description: Seven number cards, each used once, are combined with the four operations to reach five large targets. A big product is made first and then trimmed back by subtracting or adding another card, and each result is checked.
teaching_notes: One idea: multiply a big card by a small card to grow fast, then add or subtract another card to land on the target. Watch for students who use a card twice, or who use a number that is not on a card.

source: Figure it Out, Q10 (get close with cards)
video_script.why: The child multiplies and compares large numbers, and now combines cards to land on a target.
video_script.substitution: Make a big product with a large card and a small card, then add or subtract another card to land on the target; use each card once for a target.
video_script.anchor: the seven cards 4000, 13000, 300, 70000, 150000, 20 and 5 in a row, with the five targets beside them
video_script.payoff_line: Multiply to grow fast, then add or subtract to land on the target

final_answer.spoken: one lakh ten thousand, two lakh, five lakh eighty thousand and twelve lakh forty five thousand

video_script.design: One idea: multiply a big card by a small card, then add or subtract to land on the target. The cards stay in the anchor band; the working band shows each target with its values before the sums. The book's sample for the first target opens the video. No hard clear.
open_questions: The book answer key gives 12,44,500 for the fourth target (the worklist reaches 12,45,000 exactly), and uses 14 and 4 as multipliers for the last two targets, but 14 and 4 are not cards. The worklist's cards-only expressions are used instead. No search was made to show that 20,91,000 is the closest possible for the last target, so the video says only that it is 200 away.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>We have seven cards, and each card may be used once for each target.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>We can add, subtract, multiply or divide them to get close to a target.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>The first target is one lakh ten thousand.
<bookmark mark='m5'/>The book reaches one lakh thirteen thousand.
<bookmark mark='m5b'/>It uses four thousand times the sum of twenty and five, plus thirteen thousand.
<bookmark mark='m6'/>Can we do better, and how close can we get to all five targets?

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: cards: a big card times a small card grows fast; subtracting a card trims back; each card once for a target

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Multiplying a big card by a small card makes a number grow fast.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Subtracting a card trims the number back to the target.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Each card may be used only once for a target.

marks.m1: the given line is written in the working band

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Given, the cards four thousand, thirteen thousand, three hundred, seventy thousand, one lakh fifty thousand, twenty and five.

beats.on_screen: To find: an expression for each of the five targets

marks.m1: the find line is written under the given line

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>We have to make each of the five targets with these cards, as close as we can.

marks.m1: the heading the first two targets appears

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, the first two targets use a big product less the card one lakh fifty thousand.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Thirteen thousand times twenty is two lakh sixty thousand.
Take away one lakh fifty thousand, and we reach one lakh ten thousand exactly.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Seventy thousand times five is three lakh fifty thousand.
Take away one lakh fifty thousand again, and we reach two lakh.

marks.m1: the heading the third target appears

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, five lakh eighty thousand.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Four thousand plus three hundred is four thousand three hundred.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Multiplied by twenty it is eighty six thousand.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Multiplied by five it is four lakh thirty thousand.
<bookmark mark='m5'/>Add the card one lakh fifty thousand to reach five lakh eighty thousand.

marks.m1: the heading the fourth target appears

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, twelve lakh forty five thousand.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Thirteen thousand plus seventy thousand is eighty three thousand.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Twenty less five is fifteen.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Eighty three thousand times fifteen is twelve lakh forty five thousand, exactly.

marks.m1: the heading the last target appears
marks.m4: 14,06,000 + 6,85,000 = 20,91,000 is written with the gap of 200

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, the last target is twenty lakh ninety thousand eight hundred.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Three hundred plus seventy thousand, times twenty, makes fourteen lakh six thousand.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>One lakh fifty thousand less thirteen thousand, times five, makes six lakh eighty five thousand.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Together they make twenty lakh ninety one thousand, which is two hundred more than the target.

marks.m2: ticks appear beside 13000 x 20 and 70000 x 5
marks.m3: a tick appears for each target, with no card used twice

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step five, check the work.
Adding back one lakh fifty thousand gives two lakh sixty thousand and three lakh fifty thousand.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>These match the two products.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>In every target, no card is used more than once.

marks.m2: the first four targets are ticked
marks.m3: the last result 20,91,000 is underlined with 200 away

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Multiply to grow fast, then add or subtract to land on the target.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The first four targets are reached exactly.
They are one lakh ten thousand, two lakh, five lakh eighty thousand and twelve lakh forty five thousand.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The last target gets twenty lakh ninety one thousand, only two hundred away.
